s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with purulent discharge
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Purulent discharge for 10 months
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI
Opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of right upper eyelid swelling
10 months of purulent discharge
No history of trauma to the head
No symptoms of fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Node measures 11 × 7 mm
MRI shows high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
CT shows opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses
Expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses without bone destruction
Histopathology reveals mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with purulent discharge

shortlist.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: MRI and CT findings of opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus

shortlist.label: Ethmoid sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: CT findings of opacification and expansion of the right ethmoid sinus

shortlist.label: Actinomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic purulent discharge and presence of an immovable scarlike node

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate on histopathology

shortlist.label: Kimura disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling and presence of eosinophils on histopathology

shortlist.label: Angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eosinophilia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of eosinophils on histopathology and chronic eyelid swelling

shortlist.label: Orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling and purulent discharge

raw.rationale: The presence of a long-standing, immovable, scarlike node on the eyelid with chronic purulent discharge, along with histopathological findings of lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate and eosinophils, is consistent with Kimura disease, a chronic inflammatory disorder often affecting the head and neck region, particularly in Asian males but can also occur in females.

rejected.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
rejected.why: Lack of specific symptoms related to the lacrimal apparatus

rejected.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
rejected.why: No evidence of a mucocele on imaging, and clinical presentation does not match

rejected.label: Ethmoid sinus mucocele
rejected.why: Similar to frontal sinus mucocele, no evidence on imaging and clinical mismatch

rejected.label: Actinomycosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with more systemic symptoms and specific histopathological findings not mentioned

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Would expect more widespread systemic or pulmonary involvement and different histopathology

rejected.label: Angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eosinophilia
rejected.why: While it could explain some findings, the overall clinical and histopathological picture fits Kimura disease better

rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: Acute presentation and lack of chronic inflammatory signs and specific histopathological features
